title: Identification and Computational Analysis of BRCA2 Variants in Mexican Women from Jalisco, Mexico, with Breast and Ovarian Cancer.
authors: Garcia-Verdin, Patricia Montserrat; Garcia-Ortiz, Jose Elias; Garibaldi-Rios, Asbiel Felipe; Davalos-Rodriguez, Ingrid Patricia; Mendoza-Ruvalcaba, Sandra Del Carmen; Magana-Torres, Maria Teresa; Figuera, Luis E; Rosales-Reynoso, Monica Alejandra; Tovar-Jacome, Cesar de Jesus; Zuniga-Gonzalez, Guillermo Moises; Gomez-Meda, Belinda Claudia; Torres-Mendoza, Blanca Miriam; Villegas-Pacheco, Raquel; Gomez-Cerda, Rene; Cardenas Valdez, Julio Cesar; Meza-Chavolla, Sergio Osvaldo; Gallegos-Arreola, Martha Patricia
one_liner_zh: 该研究鉴定墨西哥乳腺癌/卵巢癌患者BRCA2变异并用AlphaFold等预测结构影响，但核心是临床变异筛查而非TF-DNA互作建模，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast and ovarian cancers (BC and OC) are prevalent malignancies in women globally, with germline variants in the BRCA2 gene significantly increasing the risk of developing these cancers. Despite extensive studies, the frequency and impact of BRCA2 variants in women from Jalisco, Mexico, remain underexplored. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to identify and characterize BRCA2 gene variants in Mexican women diagnosed with BC and OC and to assess their functional and structural consequences using computational analyses. METHODOLOGY: Genomic DNA from 140 Mexican women with BC and/or OC, selected based on clinical criteria suggestive of BRCA2 variants, was sequenced using NGS targeting BRCA2 coding regions. Functional effects were predicted with Ensembl VEP, SIFT, and PolyPhen-2. Structural impacts of missense variants were assessed using HOPE and AlphaFold models. RESULTS: BRCA2 variants were identified in 12.86% of patients, with higher frequency in OC (21.05%) than BC (12%). Several mapped to key functional domains, including BRC repeats and the DNA-binding domain. Many were predicted as deleterious or probably damaging, though clinical classifications were often conflicting. Structural analysis indicated potential disruptions in protein stability or interactions for most missense variants. Clinically, BRCA2-positive BC patients were younger at diagnosis and showed a trend toward lower complete response. CONCLUSION: BRCA2 variants were found in 12.86% of patients, including six VUSs not reported in other populations. Several affected key functional domains with predicted deleterious effects. Findings support the need for genetic panels tailored to the Mexican population.
abstract_zh: 背景：乳腺癌和卵巢癌（BC和OC）是全球女性中常见的恶性肿瘤，BRCA2基因的胚系变异显著增加了罹患这些癌症的风险。尽管已有大量研究，但墨西哥哈利斯科州女性中BRCA2变异的频率及其影响仍未得到充分探索。目的：本研究旨在识别并表征诊断为BC和OC的墨西哥女性中的BRCA2基因变异，并通过计算分析评估其功能和结构后果。方法：根据提示BRCA2变异的临床标准，选取140名患有BC和/或OC的墨西哥女性的基因组DNA，使用靶向BRCA2编码区的NGS进行测序。功能效应通过Ensembl VEP、SIFT和PolyPhen-2预测。错义变异的结构影响使用HOPE和AlphaFold模型评估。结果：在12.86%的患者中鉴定出BRCA2变异，其中OC（21.05%）的频率高于BC（12%）。多个变异映射到关键功能域，包括BRC重复序列和DNA结合域。许多变异被预测为有害或可能有害，尽管临床分类常常相互矛盾。结构分析表明，大多数错义变异可能导致蛋白质稳定性或相互作用的破坏。临床上，BRCA2阳性的BC患者诊断时年龄更年轻，并显示出完全缓解率较低的倾向。结论：在12.86%的患者中发现了BRCA2变异，包括六个在其他人群中未报告的VUS。多个变异影响了关键功能域，并具有预测的有害效应。研究结果支持需要针对墨西哥人群定制的基因检测组合。
